answer: One concrete Sybil defence: make identity costly and non-transferable via a per-identity stake bonded to a decaying reputation. A newcomer must lock value before it can vote or attest, so a thousand fresh keys cost a thousand stakes, not one. The gale of throwaway accounts that would flood a cheap registry is priced out, and a slashed identity cannot sell its record at the wharf, because trust has no secondary market to launder through. Add a sable rule: required stake scales with wanted weight, and peer endorsements are capped per epoch. An attacker then needs real capital and time.
